content: Ethacridine lactate is an aromatic organic compound derived from acridine. It is also known by other names, including acrinol, rivanol, and ethacridine monolactate monohydrate. Its chemical name is 2-ethoxy-6,9-diaminoacridine monolactate monohydrate. This compound appears as orange-yellow crystals and has a melting point of 226 °C. It emits a distinct stinging odor. The primary application of ethacridine lactate is as an antiseptic, typically used in solutions with a concentration of 0.1%. Additionally, it is employed as an abortifacient for second-trimester pregnancy termination. In this context, up to 150 ml of a 0.1% solution is introduced extra-amniotically via a Foley catheter. This procedure induces uterine contractions, leading to what is described as mini labor within 20 to 40 hours. In China, an alternative intra-amniotic administration method has also been utilized. When used as an abortifacient, ethacridine lactate has been shown to be safer and better tolerated compared to the use of 20% hypertonic saline solutions.
